stem: Two engineers at Tidewater Freight each run `terraform apply` for the same configuration from their own laptops, and no backend is configured. Which statement describes the genuine weakness of this setup?

choices.text: Each person's state file lives on their own disk, so each needs the latest copy first and a lost laptop loses the state
The default backend takes no lock, so two applies started on one laptop can corrupt the file
Only the default workspace is possible, so each environment needs a separate working directory
There is none: committing the state file to the shared repository gives the pair a shared, versioned copy of the latest state

rationale: The documented limits of local state are that it restricts collaboration and risks losing the state if the file is lost, because each user has to make sure they hold the latest state data and that nobody else runs at the same time. The local backend does lock its file through system APIs, so a lock-free default is wrong. The local backend has a `workspace_dir` setting for the path of non-default workspaces, so more than the default workspace is possible. Storing state in version control can lead to data loss or exposure of secrets, so committing the file is not a fix.
